overview_markdown:
## Overview

thepopebot is a self-hosted personal AI agent platform that combines a chat interface, a live coding environment, and a background job runner into a single Node.js application. Its core architecture is described as 'three doors, one brain': browser chat, Telegram (with per-user verification), and code workspaces all feed into a central event handler that picks the coding agent, manages sessions, and orchestrates Docker containers. It is LLM-agnostic (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and agent-agnostic (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, and others).

The standout differentiator is the split between **live chat** (agent runs in-process or in a headless container, streaming to your screen) and **agent jobs** (background workers that spin up fresh Docker containers, open PRs, auto-merge, and DM you on completion). This makes it closer to an autonomous junior developer than a chatbot. Recent commits show active, careful maintenance — fixing stale config caches that served outdated bot tokens, adding Telegram webhook URL overrides for proxied deployments, and tightening the admin UI.

Compared to OpenClaw, thepopebot is narrower but more opinionated: it focuses on the coding-agent-plus-chat loop rather than broad multi-channel assistant features. Everything runs on your hardware with your tokens, giving it a strong privacy posture, though unrestricted shell access via live terminals and Docker jobs means operational risk is non-trivial. Slack and Discord integrations are promised but not yet shipped.
